summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — RNO.PA +8%, DSY.PA +6%, ADS.DE +5%, WPP.L +5%, RHM.DE +5%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (HLN.L -17%, LLOY.L -5%, VNA.DE -3%, STJ.L -3%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HLN.L (-16.99%) — Likely reaction to Haleon's Q3 2026 trading statement (released 29 Oct; analysts had flagged growth near the low end of guidance). I couldn't confirm the figures or the cause of the -17% move. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: HLN.L is a large-cap UK consumer-health stock that no strategy covers. It was also a results-driven gap, and a -17% gap would likely fail gap-size filters even if it were in a universe.

top_movers.catalyst: Follow-through from Renault's Q3 results on Oct 29: revenue +1.5% to ~€11.6B, EV sales +85%, FY2026 guidance confirmed. Stock rebounded from near its 52-week low. No separate Oct 30 news found.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Renault is a Paris-listed mid-cap auto name that no strategy includes. The move was also a delayed reaction to results released the prior day, so a gap or volume trigger would have fired at the open.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large and mid-cap CAC 40/SBF 120 autos like RNO.PA to the uk-eu momentum universe. Also let the earnings-gate release names with a post-results gap of at least +5% within one session of the report.

top_movers.catalyst: Follow-through after Q3 results on Oct 28 (rev €1.55B vs €1.52B est, EPS €0.32 vs €0.31, FY26 guidance raised, life-sciences push). No same-day news found; may also be a software-sector rebound.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DSY.PA is a large-cap Euronext Paris software name that no strategy includes. The catalyst also came two days earlier, so a same-day gap or news trigger would not have fired.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU software/tech (DSY.PA, SAP.DE, etc.) to the momentum universe, and add a post-earnings drift rule that enters names up ≥3% within 3 days of a beat-and-raise print, which this setup would have met.

top_movers.catalyst: Follow-through from record Q3 (revenue +9% to €7.25B, first >€1B quarterly operating profit) and guidance raise to ~€2.5B EBIT, with analyst target hikes (Citi €211). Today's specific trigger is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: a large-cap German DAX consumer name that no strategy covers. The catalyst was also a pre-announced profit warning-style upgrade on Oct 20, so today's move was drift after the news, not a fresh gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX/Euro Stoxx 50 large caps such as ADS.DE to the momentum universe, plus a post-guidance-raise drift rule: enter on a +3% day within 10 sessions of an upgrade if price is above the 20-day MA.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely follow-through from WPP's Q3 2026 trading update (scheduled 29 Oct) after a heavily sold-off year. I couldn't confirm the actual figures or the reaction, so this is unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: WPP.L is a UK-listed mid-cap ad-agency stock that no strategy covers. If the move was a results-driven gap, it also happened after the pre-market signal window.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK/EU mid-cap 'earnings-gap' watchlist (FTSE 250 or FTSE 100 names reporting Q3) to the news-reactive universe, with a gate that releases names gapping at least +4% on a results day.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found; likely a European defence-sector bounce ahead of Q3 results due 5 Nov 2026, with no company-specific release identified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: RHM.DE is a large-cap German defence stock on Xetra, and no strategy covers it. With no discrete catalyst, a +4.5% move would also be unlikely to trip a gap or news trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU defence names (RHM.DE, BA.L, HO.PA, SAAB-B.ST) to the uk-eu momentum universe, with an entry rule such as 1-day move ≥ +4% on volume ≥ 1.5× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely Q3 2026 results: a search snippet says pre-tax profit rose 8% to about €2.6B, a third straight record quarter, on track for 2026 targets. The snippet is undated, so I couldn't confirm it is today's report.

top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HLN.L is a large-cap UK consumer-health stock that no strategy covers. It was also a results-driven gap, and a -17% gap would likely fail gap-size filters even if it were in a universe.

top_movers.suggestion: Add UK/EU financials (LLOY.L, BARC.L, NWG.L) to the universe, and make the earnings-gate flag a -4% or larger post-results drop as a mean-reversion candidate, subject to a 2-day cooldown.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found; searches returned only prior-year Vonovia results. Likely a rate-sensitive German real-estate sector move (bund yields) ahead of Q3 results in early November.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: Vonovia is a large-cap German residential REIT on XETRA, and no strategy covers it. A -3.4% drift with no news gap would also fail a news-reactive or gap filter.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for this name. If wanted, add a rate-sensitive sector basket (EU REITs) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a bund-yield move above a set bp threshold.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed news driver found for 30 Oct. St James's Place (STJ.L) has been under pressure all year from adviser/partner-firm exits (Sovereign Wealth, Prospera, Wellesley), so this is likely a continuation of that move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. STJ is a mid-cap FTSE 250 wealth manager, and no strategy lists it. A -3.3% drift with no discrete catalyst also wouldn't trip a gap or volume-spike trigger, and a long-only bot can't short it.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change. A -3% drift with no identifiable catalyst on a long-only bot isn't worth widening the universe for. A rule to watch for repeated adviser-exit headlines at FTSE 250 financials would be speculative.
